behavior: A menu frame completes through the actual renderer GPU gate before startup controls are revealed.
The next showroom submission waits 1000/15 ms after observed completion; the completion callback and at least one following callback remain free for UI painting.
Covered settings return before either frame scheduler; settings preparation may drain the same real fence without losing its owned menu handoff.
Renderer identity, reset and disposal prevent stale startup receipts; context loss and failed GPU queries do not authorize a handoff.
Driving and replay retain their existing direct GPU-gate branch; no physics, quality, scene-pass or model simplification is introduced.

causeAssessment.sourceFact: The prior idle cap measured elapsed time from submission start. On slow completion that interval had expired, permitting another full menu render in the completion callback. Startup controls were exposed at submission, before completion.
causeAssessment.traceFact: The failed controls resolved in the DOM, then waited for visible/enabled/stable actionability; no scroll or interception failure was reached. In the Apply trace the modal existed and low quality selection succeeded, but the latest screencast remained the bare menu throughout the 15-second click wait.
causeAssessment.inference: The combined evidence supports a UI-paint starvation window during menu GPU handoff. It does not measure a new GPU FPS or guarantee total startup time.
